RECAP.t: Nov 27 close (CNBC/Reuters, half-day session ending 1 p.m. ET): the Dow rose 591.99 points, or 1.18%, to 50,774.94, the S&P 500 gained 1.60% to 7,297.49 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 2.31% to 24,129.50. For the week the S&P 500 rose 5.6%, the Nasdaq 6.68% and the Dow 5.46%, as investors returned to battered AI-linked shares after Thanksgiving.

CAL: ISM manufacturing PMI and JOLTS job openings at 10:00 a.m. ET. The prior ISM reading was 55.5 and the consensus is 55.0; JOLTS is forecast at 7.45 million vs 7.52 million.
ADP November private payrolls at 8:15 a.m. ET; consensus is 80K vs 86K in October.
ISM services PMI at 10:00 a.m. ET; the prior reading was 54.5 and the consensus is 54.5.
Nonfarm payrolls, unemployment and average hourly earnings at 8:30 a.m. ET. Consensus is about +90K payrolls (vs +165K in October), unemployment 4.1% and hourly earnings +0.3%.
The Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting decision; CME FedWatch gave a 99.2% chance of a quarter-point hike to 4.00%-4.25% as of Nov. 27.

NEWS.h: Dow rallies 592 points on a half-day to end its best week since 2022; Nasdaq jumps 2.31%
NEWS.w: Per CNBC and Reuters, the Dow rose 591.99 points to 50,774.94, the S&P 500 gained 1.60% to 7,297.49 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 2.31% to 24,129.50 in a session that closed at 1 p.m. ET after Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday.
NEWS.m: For the week the S&P 500 gained 5.6%, the Nasdaq 6.68% and the Dow 5.46%, driven by buyers returning to hard-hit AI-linked shares (Reuters).
NEWS.a: Interview point: a 5.6% weekly gain right after a 3.2% intraday S&P drop shows how fast sentiment can swing; be ready to explain what drives that kind of volatility.

NEWS.h: Fed's December hike is priced in at 99.2% as the blackout period starts; the jobs report is the last big input
NEWS.w: Per Investing.com, CME FedWatch showed a 99.2% chance of a quarter-point hike on Dec. 9, which would lift the target range to 4.00%-4.25%. The Fed's blackout period began Saturday, Nov. 28.
NEWS.m: Futures gave a 60.1% chance of two hikes by the Jan. 27 meeting. Core PCE rose 3.3% in the year to October, above the 3.2% forecast (Investing.com; Yahoo Finance).
NEWS.a: Interview point: explain why a fully priced hike moves markets less than the guidance that comes with it.

NEWS.h: Puig to buy 75% of Parfums de Marly owner Artessence from Advent for about EUR 1.2 billion
NEWS.w: Per Reuters, Spanish beauty company Puig agreed to buy a 75% stake in Artessence, owner of Parfums de Marly and Initio Parfums Prives, from private equity group Advent for about EUR 1.2 billion ($1.31 billion).
NEWS.m: The deal values the whole target at $1.9 billion. Advent acquired Parfums de Marly in 2023, and a holding controlled by founder Julien Sprecher keeps the other 25% (Reuters).
NEWS.a: Interview point: this is a sponsor exit with a founder rolling a minority stake, a common structure worth knowing.

NEWS.h: Canaccord Genuity agrees to a roughly $1.6 billion take-private by its CEO, alongside a GBP 1.17 billion UK wealth sale to Centerbridge and Mubadala
NEWS.w: Per Lexpert, chairperson and CEO Dan Daviau will take Canaccord private in an all-cash deal reported at about $1.6 billion, or about $15.27 per common share, conditional on the sale of its UK wealth business to a Centerbridge and Mubadala-backed consortium for GBP 1.17 billion.
NEWS.m: A 45-day go-shop runs to Dec. 30, 2026, with a $41.6 million termination fee; closing is expected in the first half of 2027 (Lexpert).
NEWS.a: Interview point: a management buyout with a go-shop is a good example of how boards test whether the price is fair.

NEWS.h: Dow recovers a 1,100-point drop to close up 0.33% as the AI selloff eases; S&P 500 ends down 0.25%
NEWS.w: Per CNBC, the Dow rose 164.25 points to 50,182.95 after falling more than 1,100 points at its low. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62% to 23,585.80 and the S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,182.78, after being down 3.2% at its low. Materials, energy and real estate rose.
NEWS.m: The Russell 2000 gained 0.71% to 2,704.06 (MarketWatch). Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving.
NEWS.a: Interview point: explain why a big intraday drop that reverses can say more about positioning and sentiment than the closing change does.

NEWS.h: Virbac agrees to buy Paine Schwartz-backed Axiota Animal Health for $315 million in cash
NEWS.w: Virbac signed a definitive agreement to acquire 100% of Axiota, a Paine Schwartz Partners portfolio company, in an all-cash deal valued at $315 million. Axiota adds about $47 million of US revenue and a cattle-health portfolio led by Multimin and Lactipro. Closing is expected by the end of January 2027, subject to HSR antitrust clearance.
NEWS.m: Virbac says the deal should lift its adjusted EBIT margin by about 30 basis points in 2027 and about 50 basis points by 2030.
NEWS.a: Interview point: this is a private equity exit to a strategic buyer. Explain why a sponsor sells a portfolio company to a strategic buyer instead of an IPO.

NEWS.h: Marvell and Salesforce headline a light earnings week as the November jobs report lands Dec 4
NEWS.w: Per FOREX.com, Marvell reports Tuesday Dec 1 after the close against estimates of $1.10 per share on $3.15 billion of revenue, and Salesforce reports Wednesday Dec 2 after the close against $3.45 per share on $11.46 billion. Okta also reports Dec 1 after the close.
NEWS.m: Markets entered the break pricing a quarter-point Fed hike in December, so Friday's jobs report is the main data risk (FOREX.com).
NEWS.a: Interview point: explain why guidance and remaining performance obligations can matter more than the quarterly beat for a software stock.

NEWS.h: October PCE inflation hits 3.8% and Q3 GDP is revised up to 4.3%, keeping a December Fed hike near-certain
NEWS.w: Particle reports core PCE rose to 3.3% and the Commerce Department revised third-quarter real GDP to a 4.3% annualized pace on stronger consumer spending and a surge in business investment in software and AI. Financial markets have priced in a near-certain quarter-point hike at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.
NEWS.m: ABC News (a pre-release preview) put the odds of a quarter-point hike at about 97% per CME FedWatch and said a December hike would be the central bank's second in four months.
NEWS.a: Interview point: explain why strong GDP plus sticky inflation pushes the Fed toward hikes, and what higher rates do to discount rates and deal valuations.

NEWS.h: Todd Boehly's consortium signs a US-backed share swap to buy Lukoil's international assets
NEWS.w: Per Reuters, Boehly (CEO and owner of Eldridge) leads a consortium that includes the US International Development Finance Corp. It will swap Lukoil securities worth $10 billion for the international assets, which two people familiar valued at around $16 billion. The assets span 11 countries and produce around 350,000 barrels of oil a day. Closing could take up to a year and needs OFAC approval.
NEWS.m: The swapped shares go into a UAE escrow account so Lukoil gets no windfall, a structure meant to satisfy the US Treasury's sanctions on Lukoil. The DFC stake gives the US a share of future profits after private investors recover capital plus an agreed return.
NEWS.a: Interview point: explain how sanctions and regulatory approval shape deal structure, and why a share swap into escrow differs from a cash purchase.

NEWS.h: Deere forecasts fiscal 2027 net income of $4.50 billion to $5.25 billion, below the $5.91 billion analysts expected
NEWS.w: Per Reuters, Deere's fourth-quarter net income was $1.05 billion, or $3.89 a share, versus $4.05 expected, while net sales of $10.51 billion beat the $10.37 billion estimate. The forecast includes a one-time non-cash charge of $250 million to $400 million tied to a pension payout. Deere cited a subdued ag market and weak crop prices.
NEWS.m: Deere recorded $383 million in tariff recoveries in fiscal 2026, and expects construction and forestry sales to be flat to up 10%, helped by AI data center buildout.
NEWS.a: Interview point: explain why a company can beat on sales but still be marked down on guidance.

NEWS.h: US futures fall sharply before the open as Asian stocks sell off
NEWS.w: Per TipRanks as of 5:44 a.m. EST, Nasdaq-100 futures were down 2.55%, S&P 500 futures down 1.54% and Dow futures down 0.82%. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 2.78% and Shanghai fell 2.03%. Brent fell 0.54% to $90.90 and WTI was down 0.79% at $81.40.
NEWS.m: The article noted reports that the administration is preparing new tariffs on 16 major trading partners, and that US markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving.
NEWS.a: Interview point: explain what futures moves do and don't tell you about the regular session.

NEWS.h: Stocks slip as Nvidia falls 7.6% and Anthropic drops below its $83 IPO price; Dow gains 400+ points
NEWS.w: Per AP, the S&P 500 fell 0.5% Tuesday and the Nasdaq fell 1.5%, while the Dow added more than 400 points. Nvidia fell 7.6% after soaring 31.5% Monday, Anthropic fell 9.3% to below the $83 it first sold for in its IPO last week, CoreWeave sank 12.7% and GE Vernova dropped 5.5%. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.90% from 4.92%, and Brent crude rose 2.4% to $88.78.
NEWS.m: AP noted Democratic midterm wins have raised concerns about more AI regulation, including possible halts to data center construction. Dollar Tree rose 10.5% and Kohl's 15.3% after earnings beats, and consumer confidence improved more than economists expected.
NEWS.a: Interview point: explain why a stock that doubles its recovery in a day can give back gains fast, and what an IPO trading below its offer price signals.

NEWS.h: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for $175 a share in cash, about $41 billion
NEWS.w: Sanofi said Tuesday it will pay $175 per share in cash for Insmed, a roughly $41.0 billion equity value and a premium of about 17.5% to Insmed's last close. It expects the deal to close in the first half of 2027, pending Insmed shareholder and regulatory approvals, and to be accretive to earnings per share by the end of 2028.
NEWS.m: Sanofi is paying with debt and cash on hand. PharmTech called it the largest pharma acquisition on a Reuters list since Pfizer's $43 billion purchase of Seagen in 2023.
NEWS.a: Interview point: this is an all-cash deal, so the buyer funds it with cash and new debt and Insmed holders get a fixed price per share, unlike an all-stock deal.

NEWS.h: Investors expect another Fed rate hike in December as GDP and PCE inflation data land Wednesday
NEWS.w: Yahoo reported investors anticipate a further Fed increase in December after October's 25-basis-point rise, and that one governor has suggested 50 basis points could be appropriate. NY Fed President John Williams said inflation expectations remain well anchored and he expects price growth to slow to just above 2% in 2027. The Q3 GDP second estimate and October PCE both come out Wednesday at 8:30 a.m. ET.
NEWS.m: The Fed's December decision is due Wednesday Dec 9 at 2:00 p.m. ET. Forecasts for Wednesday's data vary by source.
NEWS.a: Interview point: walk through how a rate hike changes discount rates and why growth stocks and leveraged buyouts feel it first.

NEWS.h: HPE falls more than 9% premarket after a 17% jump; Dick's Sporting Goods and Best Buy rise on results
NEWS.w: Per Yahoo, Hewlett Packard Enterprise fell more than 9% premarket Tuesday after gaining more than 17% Monday, following fiscal Q4 revenue of $14.55 billion and free cash flow of $1.92 billion, both above consensus, plus a $5 billion added buyback. AP reported Dick's Sporting Goods shares up 16% on better-than-expected net income and revenue, and Best Buy up more than 6% on its strongest quarterly comparable-store sales growth in years.
NEWS.m: Premarket moves can fade or reverse by the close. Analysts flagged uncertainty about AI infrastructure spending in 2027 to 2029.
NEWS.a: Interview point: explain why a stock can fall on a beat when guidance or the prior run-up already priced in good news.

NEWS_QUIZ: The S&P 500 gained 5.6% in a holiday-shortened week. What does a move like that right after a sharp selloff most likely show?
Volatility is elevated and sentiment can reverse quickly
Large swings in both directions within days are the signature of high volatility.
Puig is buying 75% of Artessence from Advent and the founder keeps 25%. What is the founder's stake called?
A rollover or retained minority stake
Sellers who keep part of the equity are rolling over, which keeps them aligned with the new owner.
Canaccord's take-private has a 45-day go-shop. What is its purpose?
To let the company solicit competing bids after signing
A go-shop lets the board test the market for a better offer, which supports the fairness of the price.

terms: $1.7 billion transaction
Funded by Brookfield Capital Partners and Brookfield Business Corporation
PGP runs 13 furnaces at three sites in India and Sri Lanka
Overseas markets are more than 70% of sales
Closing expected in Q1 2027, subject to approvals
DEALS.what: Brookfield agreed to acquire PGP Glass, a specialty glass packaging maker, from funds managed by Blackstone Private Equity in a $1.7 billion transaction.
DEALS.why: PGP serves cosmetics, fragrance, specialty food and beverage and pharmaceutical brands in more than 70 countries, with furnace capacity above 1,800 tonnes a day.
DEALS.say: "Blackstone is exiting a portfolio company to another financial sponsor, so this is a sponsor-to-sponsor sale rather than a sale to a strategic buyer."
q: Brookfield is buying PGP Glass from Blackstone. What type of deal is it?
A sponsor-to-sponsor sale
A public tender offer
A spin-off
A merger of equals
Both buyer and seller are financial investors, so it is a secondary buyout.

terms: All-cash take-private reported at about $1.6 billion
About $15.27 per common share, a 26.7% premium to the Feb 13, 2026 close
Conditional on the UK wealth sale for GBP 1.17 billion to Centerbridge and Mubadala
45-day go-shop ending Dec 30, 2026
$41.6 million termination fee in specified cases
Closing expected in the first half of 2027
DEALS.what: Canaccord Genuity agreed to be taken private by its chairperson and CEO, Dan Daviau, in an all-cash deal, alongside the sale of its UK wealth management business.
DEALS.why: The plan revives a 2023 management-led privatization that fell apart. Shareholders need two-thirds approval plus a majority of the minority, with a special meeting expected in Q1 2027.
DEALS.say: "It's a management buyout with a go-shop, so the board is explicitly testing the market for a higher bid until Dec. 30."
q: What does a go-shop period allow?
Soliciting competing offers after signing
Raising the premium automatically
Delisting immediately
Skipping shareholder votes
A go-shop lets the target look for superior proposals for a fixed time.

DEALS.target: Artessence (Parfums de Marly owner, from Advent)
terms: 75% stake for about EUR 1.2 billion ($1.31 billion)
Values the whole target at $1.9 billion
Advent bought Parfums de Marly in 2023
Founder's holding keeps 25%
DEALS.what: Spanish beauty company Puig agreed to buy a controlling 75% stake in Artessence, the owner of Parfums de Marly and Initio Parfums Prives, from private equity group Advent.
DEALS.why: Parfums de Marly sells fragrances inspired by 18th-century French perfumery, with bottles generally priced around EUR 250 or more, giving Puig a premium niche brand.
DEALS.say: "Advent is selling a controlling stake to a strategic buyer and the founder stays in with 25%, so the founder rolls equity alongside Puig."
q: Puig buys 75% and the founder keeps 25%. What is this structure?
A control deal with a rollover minority
A full takeover
A spin-off
A merger of equals
The buyer takes control while the founder keeps part of the equity.

DEALS.target: Axiota Animal Health (from Paine Schwartz Partners)
terms: All-cash deal valued at $315 million for 100% of Axiota
Axiota is a Paine Schwartz Partners portfolio company
Adds about $47 million of US revenue
Closing expected by end of January 2027
Subject to HSR antitrust clearance
DEALS.what: Virbac, an animal health company, signed a definitive agreement on Nov 25 to buy Axiota Animal Health, a cattle-health company owned by private equity firm Paine Schwartz Partners, for $315 million in cash.
DEALS.why: Axiota brings Multimin and Lactipro and a US dairy, beef and feedlot sales team, expanding Virbac's North American footprint. Virbac expects about 30 basis points of adjusted EBIT margin improvement in 2027 and about 50 basis points by 2030.
DEALS.say: "This is a sponsor exit to a strategic buyer: Paine Schwartz sells Axiota to a company that can fold it into an existing sales network."
q: Virbac is buying Axiota from Paine Schwartz Partners. What kind of transaction is this for Paine Schwartz?
A private equity exit
A leveraged recapitalization
A spin-off
A tender offer
A sponsor selling a portfolio company to a buyer is an exit.

terms: Lukoil securities worth $10 billion swapped for the assets
Two people familiar valued the portfolio at around $16 billion
Swapped shares go into a UAE escrow account
DFC stake shares future profits after investors recover capital plus an agreed return
Needs OFAC approval
Closing could take up to a year
DEALS.what: Todd Boehly, CEO and owner of Eldridge, signed and announced on Wednesday, Nov 25 a US-backed deal to buy Lukoil's international assets through a swap of Lukoil securities, with a consortium that includes the US International Development Finance Corp.
DEALS.why: The assets cover operations in 11 countries producing around 350,000 barrels of oil per day, including oilfields in Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan and refineries in the Netherlands, Bulgaria and Romania. Boehly and a DFC official said the deal moves strategic energy assets to US or allied hands.
DEALS.say: "It's a share swap into escrow rather than cash, so Lukoil gets no windfall under sanctions, and the deal still needs OFAC approval, which is why closing could take up to a year."
q: Why does the Lukoil deal need OFAC approval?
Lukoil is under US sanctions, so the deal needs Treasury review
It is a stock-exchange rule
It is an antitrust filing for Boehly
It sets the share price
OFAC administers US sanctions, and Lukoil was sanctioned in October 2025, so the transaction needs Treasury sign-off.

terms: $175 per Insmed share, all cash
About a 17.5% premium to Insmed's last close
Funded with debt and cash on hand
Expected to close in the first half of 2027
Needs Insmed shareholder and regulatory approvals
Accretive to Sanofi EPS by the end of 2028
DEALS.what: Sanofi agreed on Tuesday, Nov 24 to buy Insmed for $175 per share in cash, a total equity value of about $41.0 billion. PharmTech called it the largest pharma acquisition on a Reuters list since Pfizer's $43 billion purchase of Seagen in 2023.
DEALS.why: Insmed brings Brinsupri (brensocatib), the first approved treatment for non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, with $1.09 billion in revenue since its August 2025 US launch through Sept. 30, 2026, plus Arikayce and a phase 3 inhaled pulmonary hypertension drug. It adds respiratory products to Sanofi's lineup.
DEALS.say: "It's an all-cash deal at a 17.5% premium, so Insmed holders get a fixed $175 and Sanofi takes on debt to fund it, which it expects to be accretive to EPS by the end of 2028."
q: Sanofi pays $175 per Insmed share in cash. What happens to the value Insmed holders receive if Sanofi's stock falls before closing?
Nothing, the cash price is fixed
It falls with Sanofi stock
It rises
It converts to shares
In an all-cash deal the target's holders receive a set price per share, so the buyer's stock price does not change their payout.

terms: Valued at about $2.9B (Tech.eu)
Taalas raised about $220M from investors including Fidelity
AMD plans to add the technology to its Instinct accelerator roadmap
DEALS.what: AMD acquired Taalas, a startup founded in Toronto in 2023 that builds chips with AI models integrated directly into silicon, in a deal Tech.eu valued at about $2.9 billion, reported November 23.
DEALS.why: Taalas designs chips around specific AI models instead of general-purpose GPUs. AMD plans to use the technology in its Instinct accelerator line.
DEALS.say: "It's a tech tuck-in: AMD buys specialized chip design talent and IP rather than building it internally."
q: AMD buying a startup's technology instead of developing it is an example of which decision?
Build vs buy
Leverage vs equity
Spin-off vs split-off
Dividend vs buyback
A strategic acquirer weighs building a capability itself against buying a company that already has it.

terms: 0.0831 New TPL shares per EagleRock Class A share
About $23.56 per EagleRock share on TPL's five-day VWAP as of Nov 20
Needs an EagleRock shareholder vote and Hart-Scott-Rodino clearance
Expected to close in the first half of 2027
DEALS.what: Texas Pacific Land and EagleRock Land (NYSE: EROK) announced a definitive agreement for TPL to acquire EagleRock in an all-stock deal with an implied equity value of about $3.0 billion, announced November 23.
DEALS.why: The companies said the deal combines complementary Permian land and water assets, adds New Mexico Delaware Basin and Midland Basin exposure, and gives TPL more water commercialization opportunities.
DEALS.say: "It's a stock-for-stock merger at a fixed exchange ratio, so the headline value is quoted off TPL's five-day VWAP and will move with TPL's share price."
q: TPL quotes EagleRock's value using TPL's five-day VWAP. What does VWAP stand for?
Volume-weighted average price
Value-weighted adjusted premium
Variable warrant asset price
Verified wholesale acquisition price
VWAP weights each trade's price by its size, smoothing out one-day swings.

terms: Enterprise value $2.65B; equity value $2.22B
1.9x EV/Sales and 18.6x EV/EBITDA on 2026 numbers
About $1.4B of 2026 revenue, mid-single-digit operational EBITA margin
Expected to close in the second half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals
DEALS.what: ABB signed an agreement to acquire Ziehl-Abegg, a maker of high-efficiency electronically commutated (EC) fans and integrated motors, at a $2.65 billion enterprise value, announced November 23.
DEALS.why: The fans add to ABB's Motion portfolio of motors and drives and broaden its offering for HVAC, industrial cooling and thermal management. ABB expects the EBITDA multiple to fall toward low double digits with synergies.
DEALS.say: "The enterprise value is $2.65B but equity is $2.22B; the difference is net debt and similar claims the buyer takes on."
q: ABB's price is $2.65B enterprise value but $2.22B equity value. What explains the gap?
Net debt and other claims ahead of equity holders
ABB's expected synergies
The HSR filing fee
A control premium
Enterprise value is equity value plus net debt and similar claims, so it is higher when the target carries net debt.

terms: 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per Zscaler share
About $260.41 per Zscaler share, a 34% premium to the last close
CrowdStrike holders would own about 84% of the combined company
Expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028
Subject to regulatory approval
CEO George Kurtz leads; Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry joins the CrowdStrike board
DEALS.what: CrowdStrike agreed to buy network security provider Zscaler for about $43.9 billion in an all-stock deal announced Monday, Nov 23. It is CrowdStrike's biggest acquisition to date and one of the largest cybersecurity deals on record.
DEALS.why: CrowdStrike secures devices and Zscaler secures networks, so the deal gives CrowdStrike a broader product set to sell to the same customers. CNBC reported analysts see it closing a gap with market leader Palo Alto Networks.
DEALS.say: "It's an all-stock deal, so Zscaler holders take CrowdStrike shares at a fixed exchange ratio and the value they get moves with CrowdStrike's stock until closing."
q: CrowdStrike pays 1.135 of its shares for each Zscaler share. What happens to the value Zscaler holders receive if CrowdStrike's stock falls before closing?
It falls too, because the ratio is fixed
It stays the same
It rises
It is converted to cash at the announced price
With a fixed exchange ratio the number of shares is set, so the dollar value moves with the buyer's share price.

terms: About $1.25B in cash, subject to customary purchase-price adjustments
Potential earnout based on Murphy's cumulative three-year performance after closing
Murphy is a mechanical contractor serving mission-critical end markets
DEALS.what: Infrastructure contractor MasTec agreed to buy Murphy Corporation, a mechanical contractor serving mission-critical end markets, for about $1.25 billion in cash, announced November 20. Sellers can earn more through an earnout tied to Murphy's performance over the three years after closing.
DEALS.why: MasTec expands its U.S. mechanical contracting work into mission-critical projects. The earnout shares risk: part of the price is only paid if Murphy keeps performing.
DEALS.say: "An earnout bridges a valuation gap: the seller thinks the business is worth more, the buyer isn't sure, so part of the price depends on future results."
q: Part of MasTec's price for Murphy depends on Murphy's results after closing. What is that called?
An earnout
A breakup fee
A tender offer
A collar
An earnout pays the seller more later if the business hits agreed performance targets.

terms: $63.25 per share in cash
Values BILL at about $6.0 billion
31% premium to the 60-day VWAP ending Nov 16
TPG takes a majority stake; Corpay a minority stake
Largest holder Starboard Value and CEO René Lacerte agreed to vote for it
Expected to close in the first half of 2027
DEALS.what: Accounts-payable software company BILL Holdings agreed to be taken private by TPG, partnering with payments company Corpay, for $63.25 a share in cash, valuing BILL at about $6.0 billion. The price is a 31% premium to BILL's 60-day volume-weighted average price before talks leaked. Founder René Lacerte stays CEO.
DEALS.why: BILL's stock had fallen far from its highs, so a private-equity buyer could pay a premium and still buy in cheaply. Corpay gets a strategic stake in a business-payments platform. TPG and Corpay used the same playbook to buy AvidXchange in 2025.
DEALS.say: "It's a take-private: TPG pays a 31% premium in cash for a fallen software stock, with Corpay as a strategic partner, betting the business is worth more out of public markets."
q: BILL's 31% premium is measured against its 60-day VWAP. Why use an average price instead of the last close?
It strips out the jump from leaked deal talks
It makes the premium look smaller
Regulators require it
It includes BILL's debt
Shares often jump once talks leak; an average from before the leak shows the real premium over the undisturbed price.

terms: $3.68B price, subject to cash, debt and working-capital adjustments
Intuit reinvests about $368M (about 10%) into new Bending Spoons shares
No financing condition; regulatory approvals required
Closing expected early 2027
Intuit agrees to a two-year non-compete after closing
DEALS.what: Intuit agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion, announced Nov 19. About $368 million of the proceeds goes back into newly issued Bending Spoons shares, so Intuit keeps a small stake in the buyer. Closing is expected in early 2027.
DEALS.why: Intuit sheds a non-core unit and keeps some upside; Bending Spoons adds another digital business. Source text is AI-generated, so check figures against the filings.
DEALS.say: "Intuit gets cash now and keeps some upside by rolling about 10% of the price into the buyer's stock, while Bending Spoons gets a scaled product to run more efficiently."
q: Intuit takes about 10% of the Mailchimp price in the buyer's new shares. What is one effect?
Intuit keeps some upside in the buyer
Intuit pays Bending Spoons
No regulatory approval is needed
The price becomes all debt
Taking buyer stock means the seller shares in the buyer's future value.

terms: 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share
All stock
~23.9% premium to Oct 28 prices
DEALS.what: Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum, a maker of lasers and optical parts for AI data centers, in an all-stock deal valued at about $115 billion, or about $1,132 per Lumentum share at Oct 28 prices. Marvell owners would hold about 67% of the combined company and Lumentum owners about 33%, with closing expected in the first half of 2028.
DEALS.why: Marvell makes chips that move data, and it wants more optical technology and factory capacity as AI data centers shift from copper to light. The companies expect more than $1 billion of yearly cost savings and say the deal should add to Marvell's adjusted EPS in the first year after closing.
DEALS.say: "Because Marvell is paying a fixed 4.5 shares, the $115 billion headline moves with its stock, so Lumentum's owners take on Marvell's share price risk until closing in 2028."
q: Marvell is paying a fixed 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share. If Marvell's stock falls before closing, what happens to Lumentum owners' payout?
It stays locked at the $1,132 headline price
It rises because Marvell issues extra shares
Its value falls because the 4.5 ratio is fixed
It converts into cash at the Oct 28 stock price
With a fixed exchange ratio, the share count stays the same, so the dollar value moves up and down with the buyer's stock.
Marvell must pay Lumentum $3.2 billion if the merger ends over certain regulatory problems. Why would Lumentum ask for this fee?
It pays Lumentum for failed-review risk
It lets Marvell skip the U.S. antitrust review
It raises the exchange ratio when deals close
It funds the $1 billion of planned cost savings
A reverse termination fee protects the target, which can lose years and business momentum if regulators block the merger.

terms: $65.00 per share
At least 75% cash
26% premium
DEALS.what: DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart's parent company, Maplebear, for $65 a share, about $17 billion of equity value. Instacart holders can choose cash, DoorDash stock or a mix, but stock is capped at 25% of the total, and the deal should close by late 2027 or the first half of 2028.
DEALS.why: DoorDash gets the leading U.S. grocery-delivery platform and its retailer software, plus a bigger ad business. Together they can offer local grocers one delivery network to compete with Walmart and Amazon.
DEALS.say: "It's a mostly-cash strategic deal funded with a bridge loan, so the key risks are antitrust review and how much new debt DoorDash takes on while trying to keep its investment-grade rating."
q: DoorDash is paying for Instacart with at least 75% cash and at most 25% DoorDash stock. What is the main benefit of the stock portion for DoorDash?
It uses less new debt and protects the credit rating
It guarantees antitrust approval from regulators
It lets DoorDash skip the shareholder vote
It locks in a lower price per Instacart share
Paying part of the price in stock means borrowing less, which helps DoorDash keep its investment-grade rating.
JPMorgan gave DoorDash a 364-day bridge loan commitment for the Instacart deal. What is a bridge loan used for?
Paying Instacart's employee retention bonuses
Covering the breakup fee if the deal fails
Short-term funding until bonds are issued later
Buying back DoorDash shares after closing
A bridge loan guarantees the cash is there at signing; the buyer usually replaces it with longer-term bonds before or at closing.
